title: Fully convolutional networks for land cover classification from historical panchromatic aerial photographs
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 167:385-395
relevance: The direct precedent for the part of our archive we have never assessed: 1936_king_rgb.tif and 1998_king_rgb.tif sit on disk and in phase4/crops but appear in no catalog entry and no config year list. It works on 1940s-50s panchromatic frames with radiometric variation between dates and locations, which is our exact problem one generation earlier, and it establishes that FCNs can classify land cover with no spectral information at all - so a 1936 extension is not obviously infeasible. Critically it also means any NDVI-like or GRVI-like feature, and the leaf-off greenness diagnostic we built in an earlier iteration, is simply undefined for those years.

title: Deep learning based individual tree crown delineation from panchromatic aerial imagery
relevance: States that NO existing tree delineation approach relies on panchromatic imagery alone because colour is considered essential, then bridges the domain gap with a deep-learning COLORIZATION step before delineation - a technique absent from all 200 papers in this tracker and a serious candidate for our pre-2000 years. It CONTRADICTS the framing behind our cross-sensor work, which has treated the historical problem as radiometric domain shift between comparable RGB sensors; for a single-band 1936 frame the gap is not a shift but a missing modality, and style-transfer methods such as FDA that assume matched channel counts cannot apply. It is also 2025, so it postdates every generalisation method currently in our plan.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Land Use and Land Cover Multi-class Maps from Historical Aerial Imagery
relevance: A second and very recent treatment of CNN land-cover mapping from historical aerial frames, useful as an independent check on Mboga because the two were produced five years apart and any agreement on achievable accuracy would give us a defensible expectation for 1936 and 1998 before committing GPU time. It matters for scoping rather than method: our temporal series currently starts at 2000, and whether it can honestly be pushed back six decades is a question about what accuracy is attainable on single-band frames, which this quantifies. Retrieved via Crossref; abstract not yet read, so the relevance claim here is provisional.
